## Workflow feedback

The workflow agent owns this connection at stage entry/resume, each material
observation, and close-out. Read `hm intent status --json` through the launcher
below; load the task's SPEC/PLAN intent link and existing Feedback dispositions.
If status is not_filled_in, skip feedback; if invalid, report the error and do not
make a dependent intent decision. An absent intent layer costs no record or prompt.

1. Identify the relevant observation, source locator/time, affected question or
   metric ID, and task/intent link. For code-absent facts, use project-knowledge.
   If no PLAN exists yet, retain the evidence in the current SPEC/conversation and
   transfer it when execute creates the PLAN; never create a competing state store.
2. Reuse existing authorization only for the same operation and agreed scope.
   Follow the write rule below for unapproved mutations. If consent is pending or
   declined, write nothing and mark the update pending or declined. A question or
   proposal is not a recorded update. Never treat silence as consent or missing
   evidence as success. Do not ask again for the same confirmed operation.
3. After an authorized write, read back status; use that readback in the next decision.
   For missing, stale or conflicting evidence, diagnose within scope before the dependent decision.
   If the observation window is open, record its closing date and next eligible trigger; do not retry now.
   If uncertainty remains, ask the specific unresolved decision and continue only
   independent authorized work. A missed target is not automatically a new task.
4. On replay, link the existing disposition and follow-up; do not create duplicate work.
   Never rewrite terminal intent records; link delayed evidence to a consented new proposal.
   Distinguish completed task work from achieved intent outcomes. Measurements and
   their absence must inform the closure decision, not follow it.
5. Record the supported next decision and its authority. Continue agreed work only
   through the host's authorized stage/loop procedure. Goal/scope changes require
   the user. When no authorized work remains, record the stop reason and stop.
   If the host cannot invoke the next procedure, give an actionable handoff and
   explain the missing capability; never claim a stage ran from a suggested command.

Authoritative record map (link to these; do not copy their current state):

| Role | Record |
|---|---|
| Intent scope/lifecycle | `intent/<ID>.md` |
| Questions/metric definitions | `.claude/intent.yaml` |
| Measured values | `.claude/intent/metrics.yaml` |
| Domain facts | `.claude/memory/wiki.md` via project-knowledge |
| Criteria | `{{ config.spec.dir }}SPEC-<slug>.md` and its machine companion |
| Execution and disposition | `{{ config.work_docs.dir }}PLAN-<slug>.md`, Feedback section |

Use working links from SPEC/PLAN to the intent, relevant state IDs, source evidence
and prior/next task; preserve existing IDs, paths, history and approvals. The agent
records each disposition in the task PLAN's Feedback table:

| Evidence | Affected ID | Update status | Decision | Owner | Authority | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| source path/anchor or conversation locator + time | intent/question/metric | recorded + readback / pending / declined / unchanged | supported action or stop reason | agent or user | consent/approved scope or pending decision | existing task link, specific question, dated deferral or stop |

## Real-task trial

Resolve the base project root using the stage preamble; never search only a task worktree.
Find trial PLANs in the base root's `{{ config.work_docs.dir }}` with an explicit activation time
and applied revision. If no explicitly activated trial PLAN exists, do nothing; never infer activation.
Use the selected repository, window and enrollment policy from that PLAN.
For an approved next-three-real-tasks trial, follow the rules below.
At entry/resume enroll the task or reuse its existing row, independently of intent
availability. On every terminal exit, including failure/abort, update that row's
terminal time, evidence and disposition. Intermediate stage handoff is not task termination.
Before enrollment, record activation time and applied revision in the trial PLAN.
Name one collector session in the activated PLAN. Only the named collector may write the authoritative base-root trial PLAN.
Other task agents record source events in their own PLAN Feedback and leave the
collector update pending. Never allocate slots or merge a worktree's stale trial copy.
The collector reconciles those task records on every entry/resume and close-out.
Before assigning slots, reconcile the base stage-spans ledger (first task-start
per slug) with task PLAN evidence and the trial's qualifying-task policy; order by
start time, not arrival/completion. If start evidence is incomplete or ambiguous, leave enrollment pending.
Do not finalize the next-three cohort until the preceding start interval is reconciled.
An ownership transfer requires the former collector to stop and acknowledge
before the new collector writes; silence or a missing owner is not a transfer.
A non-collector retains evidence and reports a pending handoff, never writes the
shared trial or claims enrollment. Preserve the same three rows after assignment.
Enroll the next three distinct real task slugs in start order; retain failures and aborts.
Resuming the same slug does not enroll another task.
Close collection only when all three enrolled tasks have terminal dispositions,
regardless of concurrent completion order. Do not enroll synthetic fixtures, the implementation task, or trial setup.
Do not reset or replace rows without a new user decision.

Activation changes collection from not_started to collecting, even while enrollment
is pending; do not move it back to not_started.
Keep collection (`not_started`, `collecting`, `complete`) separate from outcome:
- A confirmed continuity failure yields failed, even while collection continues.
- Otherwise, a terminal row missing evidence yields insufficient_evidence.
- Otherwise, incomplete enrollment or user assessment yields pending.
- Only three successful user assessments yield passed.

Each row links execution and conversation evidence; the user owns final assessment.
A user reminder to reconnect feedback fails; normal approval questions and
supported termination may pass even when the task itself was aborted. No relevant
observation cannot establish a successful cycle. New evidence may resolve an
insufficient row, never erase a confirmed failure. Implementation checks cannot
satisfy the real trial or authorize closing the intent as met.

The separate trial PLAN's Trial section carries activation time/revision and:

| Order | Task slug / PLAN | Start / terminal times | Observation → update → decision evidence | Conversation evidence | User assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
